anomalous scaling in the large deviations of Markovian systems arises from a combination of the following two conditions: (1) The system is not ergodic, and (2) the system is not Markovian.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the anomalous scaling of large deviation functions can be understood as the result of a nontrivial interplay between the time-integration of a fluctuating quantity and the time evolution of the system.
the anomalous scaling of dynamical large deviations is a generic phenomenon that is not restricted to long-range correlated processes, but can be found in a large variety of nonequilibrium systems.
the anomalous scaling is due to the nontrivial dependence of the large deviation function on the time scale.

the scaling in time of dynamical large deviations can be anomalous, ξ≠1, even in systems that do not exhibit anomalous transport, i.e., ξ=1 in the corresponding fluctuation relations.
